mainTopic: Vows against groups of people (those who rest on שבת, בני נח, זרע אברהם, Jews) and who benefits in a sale
overview: This amud has several short משניות about vows not to benefit from groups of people. In the first, a vow against 'those who rest on שבת' or 'those who eat garlic' covers Jews and כותים, but a vow against 'those who go up to ירושלים' covers only Jews. אביי explains that the משנה means people who are both commanded and actually do the מצוה. Next, a vow against 'בני נח' covers only non-Jews, because once אברהם was made holy, Jews are called by his name. A vow against 'זרע אברהם' covers only Jews: a פסוק counts the seed through יצחק, which leaves out ישמעאל, and only through part of יצחק, which leaves out עשו. A final משנה teaches how someone under a benefit vow can still buy and sell with Jews by making sure the forbidden side never gets a good deal. The גמרא tests שמואל's view, that the buyer gets the main benefit of a sale, against this משנה. It tries splitting the cases into goods nobody wants and goods in high demand, and then starts a new answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: vows against those who keep שבת, eat garlic, or go up to ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules on three נדרים against groups. Those who rest on שבת and those who eat garlic include both Jews and כותים. Those who go up to ירושלים include only Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone vows not to benefit from 'those who rest on שבת,' he may not benefit from a Jew or from a כותי. The same is true for 'those who eat garlic.' If he vows not to benefit from 'those who go up to ירושלים,' he may not benefit from a Jew, but he may benefit from a כותי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives three cases of a person who vows not to benefit from a certain group. It tells us which people count as part of each group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two groups include כותים, while the third leaves them out. The גמרא will explain why: כותים are commanded to keep שבת and actually keep it, but they do not go up to ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Samaritans, a group whose Jewish status is debated
Those who go up to ירושלים

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who vows [not to benefit] from those who rest on Shabbat —
is forbidden [to benefit] from a Jew and forbidden from Kutim.
[If he vowed] from those who eat garlic —
phrases.notes: This means people who eat garlic on Friday night, so it is another שבת-related group.

phrases.english: he is forbidden from a Jew and forbidden from Kutim.
[If he vowed] from those who go up to Jerusalem —
he is forbidden from a Jew but permitted from Kutim.
phrases.notes: כותים went up to Mount Gerizim instead of ירושלים.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who rest on שבת and those who eat garlic include Jews and כותים. Those who go up to ירושלים include only Jews.

steps.title: What does 'those who rest on שבת' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact meaning of the phrase in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the משנה mean by 'those who rest on שבת'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking what the phrase 'those who rest on שבת' really means. This sets up the next step, which tests one possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase could mean people who actually rest, or people who are commanded to rest. The answer decides who falls into the נדר.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is [meant by] 'those who rest on Shabbat'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what a key phrase of the משנה means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'those who rest on שבת' mean those who actually keep it, or those commanded to keep it?

steps.title: It can't mean people who actually keep שבת
steps.stepSummary: If the phrase meant actual Shabbat-keepers, גוים who keep שבת should be included too. So why does the משנה mention only כותים?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means people who actually keep שבת, why mention only כותים? Even גוים who keep שבת should be forbidden too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible meaning and knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the test were only whether someone actually rests on שבת, a גוי who rests would also count. The משנה names only Jews and כותים, so this meaning does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offering a possibility to test)

phrases.english: If you say [it means] from those who actually keep Shabbat,
why mention specifically Kutim?
Even gentiles [who keep it] should also [be forbidden]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading 'שובתי שבת' as anyone who actually rests.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading would also include גוים who rest, but the משנה lists only Jews and כותים.

steps.title: It means people commanded to keep שבת
steps.stepSummary: The phrase means those who are commanded to keep שבת. That includes Jews and כותים but not גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means people who are commanded to keep שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its new answer: the vow is about people who are commanded to keep שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גוים are not commanded to keep שבת, so they fall outside the נדר. This also shows that this משנה treats כותים as commanded like Jews.

phrases.english: Rather, [it means] from those who are commanded about Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading with a new definition.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'שובתי שבת' means those commanded to keep שבת. That covers Jews and כותים, not גוים.

steps.title: But כותים are also commanded to go up to ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: If being commanded is the test, כותים should also be forbidden in the ירושלים case. Yet the משנה permits them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the last case: 'from those who go up to ירושלים,' he is forbidden from a Jew but permitted from a כותי. Why? כותים are commanded to go up too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own new answer by pointing to the last case of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'commanded' is the test, it should work in every case. כותים are commanded to go up to ירושלים just like Jews. Permitting them there breaks the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the last part (of the משנה)

phrases.english: If so, say the last part [of the Mishnah]:
'From those who go up to Jerusalem' —
he is forbidden from a Jew but permitted from Kutim.
Why? But they are commanded [to go up]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the definition from step 4 using the last case of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The definition 'מצווים' (those who are commanded) from step 4.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כותים are commanded to go up to ירושלים too, so under this definition they should be forbidden. The משנה permits them.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה means people who are commanded and actually do it
steps.stepSummary: אביי says a person counts only if he is both commanded and actually does the מצוה. Jews and כותים do both for שבת. גוים who rest are not commanded. כותים are commanded to go to ירושלים but do not go.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the משנה means people who are both commanded and actually do it. In the first two cases, Jews and כותים are commanded and they do it. גוים who rest do it but are not commanded. For going up to ירושלים, Jews are commanded and do it. כותים are commanded but do not do it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by making the test two-part: commanded and actually doing. He then shows how this fits all three cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 showed that 'doing' alone is not enough, because of גוים. Step 5 showed that 'commanded' alone is not enough, because of כותים in the ירושלים case. אביי joins both requirements, and the whole משנה fits.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's groups mean people who are both commanded and actually do the מצוה. Jews and כותים fit for שבת. גוים fail because they are not commanded. כותים fail in the ירושלים case because they do not go.
steps.confusionAlert: גוים are left out because they are not commanded, even if they rest. כותים are left out of the ירושלים case because they do not go, even though they are commanded. Each group fails a different half of the test.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles how the משנה defines each group: a person counts only if he both has the obligation and actually keeps it. That one test explains all three cases of the משנה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It teaches [about one who is] commanded and does [it].
In the first two cases:
phrases.notes: These are the שבת case and the garlic case.

phrases.english: Jews and Kutim are commanded and do [it];
gentiles, those who do [it] —
do [it] but are not commanded.
In [the case of] those who go up to Jerusalem:
Jews are commanded and do [it];
Kutim are commanded but do not do [it].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5 by refining the definition from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refined definition: two requirements instead of one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being commanded alone puts someone in the group, so כותים should be included in the ירושלים case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only those who are both commanded and actually do it count. This leaves out גוים in the שבת cases and כותים in the ירושלים case.

steps.title: A vow not to benefit from the descendants of נח
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a person who vows not to benefit from בני נח may benefit from Jews but not from the nations of the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone says, 'It is קונם that I will not benefit from the descendants of נח,' he may benefit from Jews, but he may not benefit from the nations of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives a new vow case. Here the vow is against 'the children of Noah.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier vows on this daf, the question is what a phrase means in everyday speech. The משנה says 'בני נח' means non-Jews only, even though Jews also come from נח.

keyTerms.meaning: A word used to make a vow that forbids something

phrases.english: MISHNA: 'It is konam that I will not benefit
phrases.notes: קונם is a vow word. It makes something forbidden to you, the way a קרבן is forbidden for personal use.

phrases.english: from the descendants of Noah'
he is permitted to benefit from a Jew
and forbidden from the nations of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new vow phrase. It is not connected to the שבת discussion before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow against בני נח forbids benefit from non-Jews only. Jews are permitted.

steps.title: But Jews also come from נח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how Jews can be left out of 'בני נח' when they also descend from נח.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But are Jews left out of the group called 'descendants of Noah'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. Every person, Jews included, comes from נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we read 'בני נח' literally, Jews should be included in the vow and forbidden too. So the משנה's ruling that Jews are permitted needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they excluded? (literally: do they go out?)

phrases.english: GEMARA: But are Jews excluded
from the category of descendants of Noah?

steps.triggerLanguage: וישראל מי נפיק מכלל בני נח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first ruling of the משנה in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that Jews are permitted under a vow against בני נח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Jews really are descended from נח, so the literal meaning of the vow should include them.

steps.title: Jews are called by אברהם's name
steps.stepSummary: Once אברהם was made holy, his descendants became known by his name instead of נח's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since אברהם was made holy, they are called by his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that Jews are no longer called 'children of Noah.' They are called after אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow follows what people call each group, not family history alone. Once אברהם was set apart, his line got a new name. 'בני נח' was left to mean the rest of the world.

keyTerms.meaning: They are called by his name

steps.whatToRemember: A vow follows how people normally name a group. Jews are called after אברהם, so 'בני נח' means non-Jews.

phrases.english: Since Abraham was sanctified,
they are called by his name.

steps.triggerLanguage: כיון דאיקדש אברהם איתקרו על שמיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the term by how people actually name the group
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בני נח' includes everyone descended from נח, Jews too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Jews are named after אברהם, so 'בני נח' refers only to non-Jews.

steps.title: A vow not to benefit from אברהם's offspring
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a vow against זרע אברהם forbids benefit from Jews but not from the nations of the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone says, 'I will not benefit from the offspring of אברהם,' he may not benefit from Jews, but he may benefit from the nations of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case. This time the vow is against 'the seed of Abraham.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the answer in step 9: 'זרע אברהם' is the name for Jews. So only Jews are forbidden, and non-Jews are permitted.

phrases.english: MISHNA: 'That I will not benefit from the offspring of Abraham'
he is forbidden from a Jew
and permitted from the nations of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה case, the mirror image of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow against זרע אברהם forbids benefit from Jews only. Non-Jews are permitted.

steps.title: But ישמעאל is also אברהם's son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ישמעאל's descendants are not forbidden, since he is a son of אברהם.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But there is ישמעאל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that non-Jews are permitted. ישמעאל is a real son of אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'זרע אברהם' means anyone descended from אברהם, then ישמעאל's descendants should be forbidden too. The משנה lets the vower benefit from all non-Jews, so we need to know why ישמעאל is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is (a challenge pointing to a case that was left out)

phrases.english: GEMARA: But isn't there Ishmael!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'permitted from the nations' part of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the vower may benefit from all non-Jews
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ישמעאל is a biological son of אברהם, so his descendants seem to be included in 'זרע אברהם.'

steps.title: Only through יצחק is the seed called אברהם's
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק teaches that אברהם's 'seed' is counted only through יצחק, so ישמעאל is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'For through יצחק shall seed be called yours.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The name 'אברהם's seed' passes only through יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה itself defines who is called 'זרע אברהם.' ישמעאל is a son, but his line does not carry that name, so the vow does not cover his descendants.

phrases.english: 'For in Isaac shall seed be called to you' is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: כי ביצחק יקרא לך זרע כתיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ישמעאל challenge in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every descendant of אברהם, ישמעאל included, counts as 'זרע אברהם.'
steps.terutzMaskana: Only יצחק's line is called 'זרע אברהם,' so ישמעאל is excluded.

steps.title: But עשו is a son of יצחק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about עשו, who does come through יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is עשו!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. עשו is יצחק's son, so the פסוק seems to include him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said the 'seed' is counted through יצחק. עשו is a child of יצחק, so his descendants should count as 'זרע אברהם' and be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: עשו, יצחק's son and יעקב's twin

phrases.english: But isn't there Esau!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that all of יצחק's line counts as 'זרע אברהם'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עשו comes through יצחק, so by step 12's own rule his line should be included.

steps.title: Through יצחק, but not all of יצחק
steps.stepSummary: The word 'ביצחק' means only part of יצחק's children, so עשו is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In יצחק,' and not all of יצחק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the פסוק more closely. It says 'in Isaac,' meaning only part of יצחק's line, not all of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letter ב in 'ביצחק' points to only some of יצחק's children. That part is יעקב and his descendants, so עשו is excluded. This explains why the משנה forbids only Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: In יצחק, meaning part of יצחק's line

steps.whatToRemember: 'זרע אברהם' means Jews only. The פסוק counts the seed through יצחק, which leaves out ישמעאל, and only through part of יצחק, which leaves out עשו.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think ישמעאל and עשו are not really אברהם's descendants. They are. The point is only that the name 'זרע אברהם' in a vow does not cover them.

phrases.english: 'In Isaac,' and not all of Isaac.
phrases.notes: The ב means 'part of.' So only some of יצחק's children, meaning יעקב's family, are counted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the עשו challenge in step 13 and completes the explanation of the משנה in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Close reading of a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All of יצחק's children, עשו included, count as 'זרע אברהם.'
steps.terutzMaskana: Only part of יצחק's line, יעקב's descendants, is 'זרע אברהם.'
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A vow against 'זרע אברהם' covers only Jews, the descendants of יעקב.

steps.title: How to do business when a vow forbids benefit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules on three kinds of vows involving benefit from Jews, and explains how buying and selling still works under each.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone vows 'I will not benefit from a Jew,' he buys from Jews for more than the item is worth and sells to them for less. If he vows 'Jews will not benefit from me,' he buys for less and sells for more, but people won't agree to deal with him. If he vows both ways, he may benefit only from non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It explains how a person can still trade with Jews after making a vow about benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trick is to make sure the forbidden side never gets a good deal. If he may not benefit, he overpays and undersells. If they may not benefit from him, he underpays and oversells, though in real life nobody will accept such deals.

keyTerms.meaning: buys for more than the item is worth
sells for less than the item is worth
people won't go along with him
the nations of the world, non-Jews

phrases.english: MISHNAH
"That I will not benefit from a Jew"
he buys for more and sells for less.
"That Jews will benefit from me"
phrases.notes: This is short for a vow forbidding Jews to benefit from him.

phrases.english: he buys for less and sells for more,
but people do not listen to him.
"That I will not benefit from them, and they from me"
he may benefit from the nations of the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה, moving on from the זרע אברהם discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow against benefit from Jews makes him overpay and undersell. A vow against Jews benefiting from him makes him underpay and oversell. A vow both ways leaves him dealing only with non-Jews.

steps.title: שמואל: the examiner pays, so the buyer has the main benefit
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that someone who takes a vessel from a craftsman to examine it must pay if it is damaged by accident. The גמרא learns from this that he holds the main benefit of a sale belongs to the buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: someone who takes a vessel from a craftsman to examine it, and an accident happens to it in his hand, is liable. So it seems שמואל holds that the main benefit in a sale is the buyer's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling of שמואל and pulls out the idea behind it. This sets up the next move, where the idea will be tested against our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only someone who gets all the benefit, like a borrower, pays even for accidents. Since שמואל makes the examiner pay, he must see the potential buyer as the one who benefits. That shows he thinks a sale mainly helps the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: was damaged by accident, beyond his control
the benefit belongs to the buyer

phrases.english: GEMARA
Shmuel said:
One who takes a vessel from a craftsman to examine it
and an accident happened to it in his hand
is liable.
Apparently he holds
that the benefit is the buyer's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַלּוֹקֵחַ כְּלִי מִן הָאוּמָּן לְבַקְּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside ruling whose idea will be checked against the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who takes a vessel to examine it pays even for accidents, because the buyer is the main one who benefits from a sale.

steps.title: The משנה forbids selling at fair price
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from the משנה. The man who vowed not to benefit from Jews must sell for less, so selling at fair value is not allowed. Yet if the buyer gets the benefit, a fair-price sale should be fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: 'I will not benefit from a Jew' — he sells for less. So selling at an equal price is not allowed. But if the benefit belongs to the buyer, even an equal price should be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's idea using the משנה from step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seller gets no real benefit from a sale, then selling at fair price would not give the man any forbidden benefit. Since the משנה makes him sell for less, the משנה seems to think the seller does benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: equal for equal, at the fair price

phrases.english: We learned:
"That I will not benefit from a Jew"
he sells for less,
but at an equal price, no.
But if the benefit is the buyer's,
even at an equal price should be allowed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the idea pulled out of שמואל in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that the buyer has the main benefit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies that a fair-price sale benefits the seller, which goes against שמואל.

steps.title: The משנה speaks of merchandise nobody wants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is about goods that sit unsold. With those goods, the seller is the one who benefits from any sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is talking about merchandise that lies on its face.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by narrowing the case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the buyer benefits, as שמואל says. But when goods sit around and no one wants them, getting rid of them is a favor to the seller. So in that case even a fair-price sale gives the seller benefit, and he must sell for less.

keyTerms.meaning: that lies on its face, unwanted and unsold

phrases.english: Our Mishnah
is about merchandise that lies on its face.
phrases.notes: This is an expression for goods nobody wants to buy, so the seller is happy to get rid of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say every sale benefits the seller.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only with unwanted goods does the seller benefit; normally the buyer benefits, as שמואל holds.

steps.title: Then why must he buy for more?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer from the first part of the same line in the משנה. That part says he buys for more. But if the goods are unwanted, the seller is the one who benefits, so buying at fair price should be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the first part: he buys for more. With unwanted goods, why can't he just pay the fair price?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 18 using the start of the same line in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same line in the משנה says both 'buys for more' and 'sells for less,' so both must be the same kind of goods. If those goods are unwanted, then when he buys, the Jewish seller is the one being helped. So he gets no forbidden benefit, and paying extra should not be needed.

phrases.english: If so, say the first part:
he buys for more.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking: with unwanted goods, why would he need to pay extra?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן אֵימָא רֵישָׁא: לוֹקֵחַ בְּיוֹתֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה speaks of unwanted goods
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With unwanted goods the seller benefits, so the man who vowed should be allowed to buy at fair price, yet the משנה makes him pay more.

steps.title: Then why must he sell for more?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second challenge from the last part of the משנה. The man who forbade Jews to benefit from him must sell for more. But with unwanted goods, he as seller is the one who benefits, so a fair-price sale gives the buyer nothing forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, look at the last part: 'Jews will not benefit from me' — he buys for less and sells for more. But if it is about unwanted goods, even a fair price should be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second attack on the answer of step 18, this time from the last part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the Jews may not benefit from him. If the goods are unwanted, then when he sells at fair price, he is the one who benefits, not the Jewish buyer. So the משנה should not need him to charge more.

phrases.english: And furthermore, say the last part:
"That Jews will benefit from me"
he buys for less and sells for more.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added so the line matches the wording of the משנה.

phrases.english: But if it is about merchandise that lies on its face,
even at an equal price should be allowed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against the answer of step 18, added to the one in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה speaks of unwanted goods
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With unwanted goods the seller benefits, so selling at fair price gives the Jewish buyer no forbidden benefit, yet the משנה makes him sell for more.

steps.title: The last part of the משנה is about goods in high demand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from the סיפא. The סיפא is talking about goods that sell quickly. With those goods, the buyer is the one who benefits from the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last part of the משנה is talking about goods that sell fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 20. It says the last part of the משנה is about goods that are in high demand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When goods sell fast, the seller gains nothing special from a sale, and the buyer is lucky to get them. So when the man who forbade Jews to benefit from him sells, even a fair price gives the Jewish buyer a benefit. That is why he must sell for more.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of the משנה
A 'sharp' sale: goods that sell quickly because many people want them
Sharp, keen: here, in high demand

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of goods. With goods nobody wants (step 18), the seller benefits. With goods everyone wants (this step), the buyer benefits.

phrases.english: The last part is about a fast-selling sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the סיפא in step 20 by reading the סיפא as a different kind of sale than the רישא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: the רישא is about goods that sit unsold, and the סיפא is about goods in high demand.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא is about the same unwanted goods as the רישא, so selling at a fair price would give the buyer nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא is about fast-selling goods, where the buyer benefits. So he must sell for more.

steps.title: Then why must he buy for less?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the new answer. The same סיפא says this man buys for less. But with fast-selling goods the seller gains nothing, so buying at a fair price should be allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the סיפא say he buys for less? Even at a fair price it should be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 21. It uses the other half of the סיפא, which says the man buys for less.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא, the Jews may not benefit from this man. When he buys from a Jew, that Jew is the seller. With fast-selling goods the seller gets no benefit from a sale, so a fair price gives the Jewish seller nothing forbidden. So why does the משנה make him pay less?

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if what you just said is true
He buys for less than the going price
Value for value: a fair, normal price

phrases.english: If so, why does he buy for less?
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same line in the סיפא: the man whom Jews may not benefit from buys for less.

phrases.english: Even at a fair price it should be allowed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 21 from the other half of the very same line it tried to explain.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the סיפא is about fast-selling goods (step 21).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With fast-selling goods the seller gets no benefit. So when this man buys from a Jew, a fair price gives the Jew no benefit, and 'buys for less' should not be needed.

steps.title: Rather: the גמרא starts a new answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the last answer and opens a new way to explain the משנה. The new answer comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup word. The גמרא is pulling back from its last answer and getting ready to give a new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that the answer in step 21 could not explain the whole סיפא. The real new answer comes right after this word.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: we drop the last idea and say something new

phrases.english: Rather,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives up the answer of step 21 because of the challenge in step 22, and opens a new answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new answer replaces the old one. It comes on the next amud.
